primary_claim: In open-weight models, concept-injection 'introspection' reports are better explained by injection-induced entropy that compresses the YES/NO logit gap toward zero (raising 'yes' rates even on unrelated factual questions) plus 'concept leakage' from the still-active steering vector, than by genuine introspective access: the introspection score averaged across 14 models is ~0 (mean +0.013, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.), and a concept-mismatch test finds no model with a statistically significant congruent-minus-incongruent detection gap.

effect.metric: introspection score (delta-logit-detection minus delta-logit-factual), averaged across models
effect.value: mean +0.013, median -0.032, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.; individual models range from +4.14 (Qwen-1.7B) to -2.83 (Qwen-32B)

contradicts_or_qualifies: qualifies/extends Anthropic's (2025) interpretation that models 'introspect' when detecting injected concepts (~20% success for Claude Opus 4/4.1), finding this is better explained by injection-induced entropy compression and concept leakage rather than genuine introspective access
argues Anthropic's existing yes/no rate control is a weaker test than comparing baseline-corrected YES/NO logit differences, since probability is a nonlinear function of logits
stated_future_work: test whether concept injection more generally increases entropy over the next-token distribution outside YES/NO prompts (e.g. multiple-choice, factual completions with more than two plausible answers)

distinguish mechanisms behind compression by measuring full-distribution entropy, KL divergence from the no-injection distribution, and logit margins among top tokens, varying by layer, strength, and vector norm
control for or alter the inverted detection question to test the compression hypothesis more cleanly, since the inversion experiment is noisy
replicate these results in larger open-weight and larger closed models, especially the models used in Anthropic's original experiments
limitations_stated: the entropy/compression hypothesis is a behavioral signature at the output-logit level; a stronger version would test whether it appears outside YES/NO prompts
the mechanism behind compression is unclear (off-manifold degradation vs selective concept-boosting vs layer-dependent effects)
the inversion experiment is noisy: some models behave exactly as the compression story predicts, others show prompt-specific behavior
these results should be replicated in larger models; not done here due to compute limitations
scope is limited: results don't show open-weight LLMs cannot introspect whatsoever, just that this one proposed route (concept-vector injection) is heavily confounded in this setup
quote: Computing the introspection score for all models, I find that overall the introspection score is ~0 (mean +0.013, median -0.032, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.)
